findings.description: Damayantī is explicitly bhāryā, Nala’s wife. Padmahasta is explicitly amātya, minister, in52.9; he is not a named son. Former-life jāyā/apatya family is unnamed52.22 and distinct from current spouse. No Vīrasena, Bhīma, Indrasena/Indrasenā or other epic genealogy imported.

Brahmā fashions Damayantī from selected essence and gives beauty of women in the three worlds. The graph correctly distinguishes this cosmological creation description from ordinary parenthood and from a personal boon request/grant scene.

The evidence and event limited to52.1–9 include Padmahasta tall like Meru/deep like ocean, but those words occur52.10. The role and Bṛhaspati/Aṅgiras comparisons are within9; only the final physical comparisons are out of range.

recommended_action.preferred: Move the Meru/ocean clause from gup4-e-013/event013 to gup4-e-014/event014 (existing10–20 span), and add e014 as additional support to Padmahasta entity if those traits are kept there.
recommended_action.alternative: Extend both first passage and evidence to52.1–10, retaining existing IDs and an explicit locator change.
recommended_action.no_role_correction: Padmahasta minister relation itself is supported at52.9.

findings.description: Current Nala honors Gautama, who explains the former life. The former poor/pure/knowledgeable kṣatriya is unnamed, in Pippala beyond Gauṇḍadeśa; he meets and is instructed by Kauśika/Kaushika. Current Gautama and prior Kauśika are kept distinct; Kauśika is not guessed to be another named sage. No named current or former parents/adventures added.
Existing e015 gives prior-birth identity to current Nala. The explicit death-and-birth-as-Nala statement occurs52.41 in e017; add e017 to make reborn_as trace directly to the narrated transition.

recommended_action.note: Current assertion is supported contextually by the former-birth dialogue, so this is an exact-locator strengthening, not a claim reversal.

findings.description: Wife/children/friends’ harsh words cause night departure without consulting them. Kaushika compassionately blesses Gaṇeśa’s auspiciousness. The sufferer asks wishes, poverty removal, enjoyment/liberation; teacher directs one MONTH of earthen-image worship by previously stated procedure and daily story hearing, promising siddhi. The graph does not claim an explicit personal Gaṇeśa boon here.

Power012 mechanism includes poverty relief, but sole e016 covers29–35, where teacher states vow/siddhi. Explicit poverty-removal context is the sufferer’s request in28/e015. Include that context or narrow the mechanism to the teacher’s stated success promise.

recommended_action.alternative: State promised siddhi through the month-long vow, with poverty relief retained as requested purpose/context rather than a separately quoted donor promise.

findings.description: With Kauśika permission, former self returns HOME and begins bright Śrāvaṇa fourth vow. Constant Gaṇeśa meditation during standing/speech/silence/movement/sleep/eating; wealth of elephants/chariots/horses/cattle/servants, donations, costly Gaṇeśa temple, pleasures, death, then Niṣadha birth as Nala. Temple belongs to unnamed prior self, not a newly invented construction by current Nala. No supernatural instantaneous house transformation from Kardama51 is inserted.

After Gautama leaves, Nala trusts his explanation, makes an image, performs vow, hears story and worships daily, obtaining all wishes. This is current-life repeated practice, not an automatic yearly renewal rule or an imported dice/exile episode. Chapter terminal46 and colophon seen. Whole bounded narrative can remain COMPLETE after range corrections; no unresolved narrative semantic omission found in this sample.

Brahmā practices a full100years for creation, worships with services/gems/fruits and gives the two maidens Siddhi/Buddhi described as manasā kalpite. Mental-creation relationships and gift wording supported. No ordinary biological daughterhood or explicit marriage rite is stated here. Gaṇeśa gives one-syllable vidyā and Brahmā then creates; no seed string inferred.

Viṣṇu’s six-akṣara worship and a complete ONE YEAR image-vow with rules are explicit. Receiving a boon then preserving the world is a retrospective divine precedent; it is separate from the poor kṣatriya’s one-month vow and Brahmā’s100years. No DIVINE-year qualification supplied in these verses.
